target_customer: Biotech, diagnostics and pharma teams running bioinformatics and multiomic analysis who need HIPAA compliant cloud tooling
problem: Genomics tools and algorithms are hard to access and costly to operate, so scientists lose time standing up and managing compute for analysis.
business_model: B2B SaaS running in the customer's own cloud with usage transparent pricing

founders.name: Hugo Lam
education: Cambridge Judge Business School (affiliations stated on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Over 20 years in bioinformatics and genomics with 40 plus papers per the YC profile.

competitors.name: Seven Bridges
competitors.what: Cloud genomics analysis platform with HIPAA controls
competitors.traction_then: Powered the NCI Cancer Genomics Cloud

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating provisioning of cloud compute inside customer accounts and wrapping bioinformatics pipelines under HIPAA controls is standard cloud engineering with domain heavy parts.

defensibility.rationale: Established platforms such as Seven Bridges and DNAnexus already offered compliant cloud analysis, and the pitch relied on price and operation transparency.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Its intellectual property ended up with GaudiBio per its own website; PitchBook lists the company out of business in November 2025.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites high cost and access barriers in genomics for diagnostics and pharma, with testimonials from small biotech users. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses hypahub.com, which now shows a notice that it no longer offers services.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found; sources were limited to directories and the company's own pages.

outcome_analysis: HypaHub sold a HIPAA compliant bioinformatics platform to small biotech teams but was a six person company against established platforms. The company's site now says it no longer offers products as an independent company and that its IP was acquired by GaudiBio, while PitchBook marks it out of business in November 2025. The cause of the wind down is not public, and no funding beyond accelerator money was verified.
notes: Status conflict: YC lists Acquired and the company site says IP was acquired by GaudiBio, while PitchBook lists Out of Business (18 Nov 2025). A search for GaudiBio acquisition coverage found nothing, so exit date and terms are unknown. Funding unverified: CB Insights lists about 500K across two rounds, a convertible note dated 2022-03-29, with Y Combinator and StartX; aggregator only, so no rounds recorded. Only one dated competitor found. Completeness pass: a convertible note dated 2022-03-29 is recorded from CB Insights alone, a single database, with the amount left null because the total of about 500K over two rounds does not isolate the note.
